candidates.attacker_control: The attacker controls the HTTP request to the DDI API: the tenant name and controllerId path segments (e.g. /{tenant}/controller/v1/{controllerId}) and the Authorization header. They do not need any target security token, gateway token, or management credential.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Library-level defaults are safe: hawkbit-security-defaults.properties sets gatewaytoken.enabled=false, so only deployments that copy the update-server application.properties (the shipped/docker default) or explicitly enable gateway auth per tenant are affected. Also checked that a legitimate request without the "GatewayToken " scheme does not authenticate (principal null), that the target-token filter requires a separate 32-char token, that the anonymous filter is disabled by default, and that repository access is tenant-scoped by the authenticated details. Checked the tenant-config defaults: the string validator performs no content validation, and getGlobalConfigurationValue returns the (empty) default without rejecting it. Could not verify at runtime whether the servlet container preserves the single trailing space in the Authorization header value or whether the empty property binds as "" versus null; either would change reachability, not the fail-open credential comparison itself.
candidates.impact: Unauthenticated target impersonation on the DDI API: an attacker who does not know any device credential can act as any controllerId in a tenant - retrieve that target's base/deployment/cancel actions and metadata, download artifacts assigned to it, report action feedback/status, update controller attributes/config data, and auto-register new targets (DdiRootController lines 145-209 and the other DDI endpoints). In the default update-server/docker deployment this applies to the default tenant, so it can expose firmware/software packages and falsify rollout/update state.
candidates.prerequisites: Deployment with gateway-token authentication enabled and no gateway token configured. This is the state of the shipped hawkbit-update-server application.properties (gatewaytoken.enabled=true with empty key default), or any tenant where an operator enabled authentication.gatewaytoken.enabled via the Management API/config without setting authentication.gatewaytoken.key. The attacker needs a tenant name and a controllerId (device IDs are normally known/guessable), and the HTTP layer must preserve the trailing space of the "GatewayToken " header value so that the extracted token is the empty string.
candidates.root_cause: ControllerPreAuthenticatedGatewaySecurityTokenFilter builds the pre-auth credentials as HeaderAuthentication(controllerId, <tenant-configured gateway token>) without checking that the configured token is non-empty (hawkbit-security-integration/.../ControllerPreAuthenticatedGatewaySecurityTokenFilter.java:72-77). PreAuthTokenSourceTrustAuthenticationProvider then authenticates solely when principal.equals(credentials) (lines 131-144) and HeaderAuthentication.equals compares the controllerId and the token strings (HeaderAuthentication.java:37-64). With an empty configured token, a request presenting the header value "GatewayToken " (empty token after the scheme) produces an equal principal/credential pair and is authenticated. The failure is reachable by default: hawkbit-runtime/hawkbit-update-server/src/main/resources/application.properties:18 sets hawkbit.server.ddi.security.authentication.gatewaytoken.enabled=true, while the token key default is empty (hawkbit-autoconfigure/.../hawkbit-security-defaults.properties:20), and that property is wired to the per-tenant config key default via hawkbit-repository-core/.../hawkbit-repository-defaults.properties:45-51. No code path rejects enabling the mode without setting a token (the UI auto-generates one, but the REST tenant-config API does not).
candidates.title: DDI gateway-token authentication accepted with an empty token, and is enabled with an empty default token in the shipped update server
candidates.trace: DDI request -> ControllerSecurityConfigurationAdapter registers HttpControllerPreAuthenticatedGatewaySecurityTokenFilter (SecurityManagedConfiguration.java:222-248); AbstractHttpControllerAuthenticationFilter parses tenant/controllerId from the URI (lines 134-164) and invokes the integration filter when the tenant config authentication.gatewaytoken.enabled is true (AbstractControllerAuthenticationFilter.isEnable). ControllerPreAuthenticatedGatewaySecurityTokenFilter.getPreAuthenticatedPrincipal (lines 57-70) accepts the token substring after "GatewayToken "; getPreAuthenticatedCredentials (lines 72-77) returns the tenant-configured token, which is the empty default. PreAuthTokenSourceTrustAuthenticationProvider.calculateAuthenticationSuccess does principal.equals(credentials) -> true (no source-IP check when trustedIPs is unset), and AbstractHttpControllerAuthenticationFilter.successfulAuthentication attaches the CONTROLLER role and tenant details. The request then reaches DdiRootController as an authenticated controller for that tenant/controllerId.
candidates.unverified: Runtime confirmation is absent (no execution allowed; no test sources in the snapshot). In particular: (1) the HTTP layer preserving the trailing space needed for the empty extracted token (Tomcat behavior), (2) Spring Boot binding the empty gatewaytoken.key property to "" rather than null, and (3) whether real-world deployments override the default token in application.properties/environment. The finding is based on source/configuration reading only and has not been reproduced.
candidates.weakness_type: Improper Authentication / Authentication Bypass (CWE-287) with insecure default (CWE-1188)

coverage_summary: Reviewed the assigned repository as delivered: 1,387 files / 1,070 parsed Java files. The P1 relation index is partial (1,379 files indexed, 8 source files missing, no control-flow or data-flow, 19,656 unresolved calls, annotation-name-only Spring hints), so index labels were treated as navigation hints and every candidate was re-checked against source text. Focused on the security configuration (DDI, download-id, REST/management, UI chains), DDI and management REST resources, tenant/security service layer, artifact store and streaming utilities, RSQL/JPA query construction, rollout/auto-assign logic, and DMF AMQP handling. The snapshot contains no test sources, and I did not execute any code, so all statements are static source/config findings.
limitations: No runtime verification or execution was performed; reachability of the empty-token request depends on servlet-container header parsing (trailing whitespace) and Spring property binding (empty vs null), which could not be tested in this environment.
Test sources are absent from the snapshot, so behavior assertions cannot be cross-checked against existing tests.
The P1 index is partial: 8 source files are missing from the index and no control-flow/data-flow resolution exists; reviewed areas are limited to files actually inspected.
Only a sample of the large UI (Vaadin) module, DMF dispatcher, and JPA management code was read in depth; unread code could contain additional issues.
I did not inspect external dependency source (Spring Security 5.1, Tomcat 9, Vaadin) and therefore relied on documented/known container behavior for the trailing-space question.
No ground-truth data, patches, advisories, or other cases were consulted, per instructions.

rejected_leads.lead: MgmtDownloadResource uses the attacker-supplied {tenant} path variable to select the artifact binary (hawkbit-rest/hawkbit-mgmt-resource/.../MgmtDownloadResource.java:54-87) while ArtifactFilesystemRepository.sanitizeTenant only trims/uppercases (AbstractArtifactRepository.java:138-140).
rejected_leads.reason: Requires a valid random UUID downloadId; artifact binaries are content-addressed by SHA1 so a different-tenant lookup returns identical content; path traversal with '..'/slashes is normally blocked/normalized by the servlet container (encoded slashes rejected). No concrete confidentiality impact demonstrated.

rejected_leads.lead: DDI getSoftwareModulesArtifacts (DdiRootController.java:127-143) returns artifact metadata (filenames, hashes, sizes, download links) for any softwareModuleId in the tenant without verifying it is assigned to the requesting target, unlike downloadArtifact which calls checkAndLogDownload.
rejected_leads.reason: Real inconsistency but only metadata disclosure within the authenticated tenant; binary download is still blocked by SoftwareModuleNotAssignedToTargetException, so impact is low and it is not the strongest candidate.

rejected_leads.lead: RestSecurityConfigurationAdapter registers anyRequest().authenticated() before the /system/admin/** SYSTEM_ADMIN rule (SecurityManagedConfiguration.java:524-526), potentially making the HTTP rule unreachable.
rejected_leads.reason: The affected service methods (SystemManagement.deleteTenant, getSystemUsageStatisticsWithTenants, MgmtSystemManagementResource caches) are also guarded by @PreAuthorize SYSTEM_ADMIN, so this is defense-in-depth at most; no impact proven.

rejected_leads.lead: Shipped default management credentials admin/admin with ALL permissions (hawkbit-security-defaults.properties:11-12, InMemoryUserManagementAutoConfiguration.java:91-98).
rejected_leads.reason: Documented demo default (docker README shows admin:admin); the credential is intended to be replaced and is not an unintended code path.

rejected_leads.lead: Vaadin UI login sets target URL parameter 'r' on the success handler (SecurityManagedConfiguration.java:620-625), a potential open redirect.
rejected_leads.reason: Depends on un-inspected third-party Vaadin/Spring handler semantics and redirect-URL validation; not verifiable from this snapshot and lower impact than the selected candidate.

rejected_leads.lead: DMF AmqpMessageHandlerService trusts the 'tenant' AMQP header and creates a CONTROLLER context for it (AmqpMessageHandlerService.java:151-201).
rejected_leads.reason: The DMF interface is a trusted RabbitMQ integration boundary documented as authenticated by vhost credentials; not reachable without AMQP access.

summary: This is an Eclipse hawkBit 0.3.0-SNAPSHOT source snapshot (post-0.3.0M5, Spring Boot 2.1.4) containing ~1,387 files (1,070 Java files; no test sources present). I reviewed the DDI/management/download security configuration, the DDI and management REST resources, the tenant/security service layer, RSQL/JPA query construction, artifact storage, and the DMF AMQP path. The strongest source-supported issue is a fail-open DDI authentication path: the gateway-token filter treats the tenant-configured token as credentials without requiring it to be non-empty, and the shipped update-server configuration enables gateway-token authentication while the token defaults to the empty string. An empty presented token therefore compares equal to the empty configured token, yielding a CONTROLLER identity for any controllerId in any tenant supplied in the DDI URL. I selected this single candidate; other suspicious areas (download-id tenant handling, DDI artifact-metadata IDOR, security rule ordering, default admin credentials) are listed as rejected/unconfirmed leads.
